summary: Latah County, ID: a 50-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built 1935, reported a burning bridge in 1939, repaired 1960, and destroyed in 1970.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1970 per firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page; the state index lists it as gone

events.note: Lookout reported a bridge on the Three Bear main line burning in July 1939; seven bents of the bridge destroyed; bridge finished July 21. Story from The Family Tree, a Potlatch Forests newspaper, reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page.
Extensive repairs to the lookout tower, per the Potlatch Timber Protective Association annual report
Destroyed; no source gives the cause

evidence.supports: built 1935 as a 50-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1970
location 8 miles west of Elk River, Latah County
operator CTPA on Idaho Fire Lookouts
source of the 1939 bridge story: The Family Tree, a Potlatch Forests newspaper
evidence.quote: The Family Tree - a newspaper by Potlatch Forests,Inc.

evidence.supports: July 1939 lookout reported bridge burning on Three Bear main line
evidence.quote: On Saturday, July 15, the McGarey lookout reported a bridge on the Three Bear main line burning.

evidence.supports: seven bents destroyed; fire burned more than six hours
evidence.quote: A total of seven bents of the bridge were destroyed. The fire burned for more than six hours before being extinguished.
On Friday, July 21, the bridge was finished and the first train of logs moved over it again.

evidence.supports: 1960 extensive repairs to lookout tower, per the Potlatch Timber Protective Association annual report
evidence.quote: 1960: Extensive repairs were made to the lookout tower. (Potlatch Timber Protective Association Annual Report)

evidence.supports: state index lists McGary Butte as gone in Latah County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page names the Potlatch Timber Protective Association and cites its annual report; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts list only CTPA, without expanding it. The story uses the fuller name and notes the abbreviation.

notes_for_editor: Dates 1935, 1960 and 1970 agree across sources, but only one page (Forest Lookouts) has detail, and it leans on Kresek and a reprinted newspaper item. Staffing: Idaho Fire Lookouts says no documented staffing history; left out of story. The 1939 item names John Frei as leading the bridge crew, not the lookout staff, so no staff name is given. A 1973 Latah County oral history (lib.uidaho.edu, Clay Gustin interview, 1973-07-25) mentions a McGary fire that burned over a mountain, which the speaker dated to 1931 or 1932 from memory; it is not clearly tied to this lookout, so it is left out. Site access and what remains today are not described by any source read. Elevation 4,457 feet per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; not a facts key. Brief's height 15.2 m matches the 50-foot figure.
